findings.reason: as written, done-when (3) can fail for a reason neither clause measures, so the plan must either bound the loop wall or lift the test timeout explicitly, and that decision belongs in §3.
findings.text: done-when (1) permits the CPU cold compile to take up to 600 s, while done-when (3) requires `test_census_neighbour_proposals_keep_saddles_across_coarse_ties` at 500 cells to pass against an empty operand store; that test carries `@pytest.mark.timeout(900)` (tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py:2911) and the cold compile happens inside it (`tie_probe.build` -> `lean_map.jets.build_jets` -> `read_route.jets.build_jet_matrix`), so at the allowed compile ceiling only 300 s remain for the jet build loop and the census reads, and the section's own comment records that loop holding 378 GB for a further ~11,000 s at 2,132 nodes — the two clauses conflict at their own stated numbers and a worker cannot tell whether to bound the loop or raise the timeout

findings.reason: the gate's replacement sizes are the measurement, so a cell/node slip makes the node run a different experiment and report a bound that cannot be compared to the row it came from.
findings.text: done-when (1) states the low arm as "at 282 and 2,132 nodes", but §0 row 44 measures that arm as "same build, 282 cells, operand cache bypassed — 79 GB peak" and §3's own body (line 63) says "the same at 282 cells"; the 282 figure is a cell count in the evidence the ≤64 GB bound is derived from, so the clause as written sends a worker to build a 282-node program that reproduces neither the 79 GB row nor the 381 GB row, and it fixes one 64 GB bound across two arms §0 records at 79 GB and 381 GB

findings.reason: the plan states its own done-when is insufficient and does not amend it, so the builder's gate omits the one measure the recorded failure produced.
findings.text: §3's own comment at line 95 records that "the node that builds §3 should also report the loop's wall per batch, so a bounded compile is not followed by an unbounded run", and the commit that added it (9dc843919) repeats that requirement in its message, yet no done-when clause carries it; the three clauses measure compile wall, row agreement and the census test, so a node closing §3 on them can declare a bounded compile while the unbounded post-compile loop that actually outlasted a five-hour wall goes unmeasured

findings.reason: four of the section's six code citations now open on blank or unrelated lines, so the plan needs a citation refresh even though each symbol still resolves by name.
findings.text: the four `nova/equilibrium/fixed_points.py` citations are stale by two lines: the plan says `_row_program` at :389, `_source_jets` at :204, `maintain_rows` at :411 and the call at :476, while grep resolves them at :391, :206, :413 and :478, the drift introduced when commit b6bbf445d (2026-10-22) added two docstring lines above them; §3's two `scripts/prototypes/read_route/jets.py` anchors (:229, :321) still resolve exactly, which shows the owner file moved rather than the section being misread
